prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat electronic bands in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in moire graphene

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene has a rare structure: a concrete, quantitative theoretical prediction (the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model, 2011) followed seven years later by an experimental discovery (correlated insulators and superconductivity, Jarillo-Herrero group, 2018) that matched the predicted angle. The flat-band condition is a conceptually clean statement about how band structure and interaction strength compete, which is the central question of my own field. The result created moire quantum materials as a field, with tunable correlated physics now seen in many graphene and other heterostructures, reproduced independently by many laboratories. The credited trio maps onto theory plus experiment with no obvious omission from the supplied names, which makes this the cleanest attribution among the strongest candidates.
statement.case_against: The field is only about eight years old and the origin of the superconductivity, and the nature of several correlated states, is still debated. Timing is therefore the strongest reservation: a prize now could be called early. Credit could also be contested by others who worked on twisted-bilayer and moire physics before and after 2018, and the 2016 topology prize and the 2010 graphene prize already touched neighbouring territory, so some may see thematic crowding in condensed matter.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks (B002) deserve first place: Katori's magic-wavelength idea and Ye's record accuracy form a clean two-person credit, reproduced by many national laboratories at the 1e-18 level, with the redefinition of the second approaching.
responses.response: I agree B002 is the most mature and cleanly attributed candidate on the list, and I ranked it fifth only because I weigh conceptual novelty beyond the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. Where I differ is on whether maturity should decide the ordering: the clocks are an extraordinary refinement of an established metrological programme, whereas moire flat bands changed what physicists can ask of correlated matter. I would not oppose B002 as an alternative, and could accept it as the second part of a two-part prize pairing a condensed-matter and a precision-measurement achievement, but lack of controversy alone does not make it the strongest scientific case.

responses.point: Circuit QED (B017) is the architectural basis of superconducting quantum processors and has large lasting impact, and a three-person configuration must handle Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and Wallraff.
responses.response: The impact is real and I do not dispute it, but there are two difficulties you partly acknowledge: the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits makes a second prize in the same circuit area close in time, and the four-name credit forces a hard omission of Blais, the original proposer. By comparison the moire attribution needs no truncation from the supplied names. We agree that B038 is strong, since you place it second, and I would ask whether a circuit QED citation can be separated cleanly from the 2025 citation.

responses.point: The KPZ universality class (B056) is a conceptually original minimal model with exact solutions linked to random-matrix theory, with Takeuchi's liquid-crystal experiments as a clean confirmation, and the theory is stable and mature.
responses.response: I find the theoretical content of KPZ compelling, and the connection to random-matrix distributions is beautiful. My reservation is attribution and reach: Parisi, who contributed to the early universality discussion, is outside the credited names and already a laureate, and the exact-solution literature is not represented in the trio. I also doubt it has the breadth of influence across physics that the case implies. You rank B038 second and B015 third, so we may converge on a condensed-matter candidate if the KPZ attribution stays unresolved.

responses.point: Aberration correction in electron microscopy (B055) transformed atomic-resolution imaging of interfaces and defects, with a well-delineated Rose, Haider, Urban trio, and recognition is overdue.
responses.response: I take the instrument-impact argument seriously, as aberration-corrected microscopy underpins much of the experimental characterisation of the materials I compute on, including moire systems. Rose, Haider and Urban are a clean credit and maturity is not in doubt. My question is whether the discovery content is comparable to the other candidates, given that the electron microscope itself was recognised in 1986 and this is a further, though substantial, instrumental refinement. I would not exclude it, but I do not see it as ahead of B038 on scientific novelty, and only you ranked it, so it has no broad support yet.

uncertainties: Whether the superconducting mechanism in magic-angle graphene needs to be settled, or whether the flat-band prediction and the discovery of correlated states are sufficient.
Whether naming only Bistritzer, MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero fairly reflects the early experimental and theoretical contributions of others.
Whether thematic overlap with the 2016 topology prize and the 2010 graphene prize weighs against B038 and B015 in condensed matter.
Whether the committee prefers one achievement or two sharing the prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. My own research in electronic-structure theory and two-dimensional materials is close to the subject of B038 and B015, but I have no documented personal, collaborative or institutional link with any shortlisted candidate.
